common_name: Mountain Mist Dianthus (Large-Flowered Fragrant Cheddar Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral, dry, rocky to sandy soil in full sun; Mountain Mist is a large-flowered cheddar pink selection valued for showier spring bloom than most cultivars of the species.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Mountain Mist is a large-flowered cheddar pink selection, producing single, soft pink, fringed blossoms carrying a strong clove fragrance held above a dense, low mat of fine, silvery-blue evergreen foliage. Its individual flowers are notably larger than many cheddar pink cultivars, giving a showier spring display, and it shares the excellent heat and drought tolerance of the species once established in lean, rocky soil. Shear lightly after the main bloom flush to keep the foliage mat tidy and encourage repeat flowering.

common_name: Frosty Fire Dianthus (AAS-Winning Dwarf Fringed Red Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Frosty Fire is an All-America Selections-winning dwarf pink grown for its frosty silver-blue foliage and vivid red flowers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Frosty Fire is an All-America Selections-winning dwarf pink bearing an abundance of single, fringed, vivid red flowers held just above a compact mat of frosty, silver-blue foliage, the icy foliage color giving the cultivar its name and providing contrast to the intensely colored blooms. It carries the classic sweet clove fragrance of garden pinks and blooms heavily over a relatively compact, tidy habit well suited to the front of a border or rock garden. Shear lightly after the main spring flush to keep the mat dense and encourage a second round of bloom.

common_name: Amazon Neon Purple Dianthus (AAS-Winning First-Year-Flowering Perennial Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Amazon Neon Purple is an interspecific sweet william bred to flower the first year from an early seed start.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Amazon Neon Purple is an interspecific Sweet William bred for large, electric violet-purple flower clusters with a vivid, glowing intensity uncommon among traditional sweet williams, blooming the first year from an early seed start rather than requiring a full season of vegetative growth like heirloom biennial types. Individual florets carry a light, sweet fragrance and open over a long season from late spring into summer with deadheading. As a short-lived perennial it often performs best treated as a two- to three-year planting, refreshed periodically from new starts.

common_name: Amazon Neon Cherry Dianthus (AAS-Winning First-Year-Flowering Perennial Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Amazon Neon Cherry is an interspecific sweet william bred to flower the first year from an early seed start.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Amazon Neon Cherry is an interspecific Sweet William producing dense, rounded clusters of bright cherry-red flowers with an intense, glowing color saturation, blooming the first year from an early seed start unlike traditional biennial sweet williams that need a full season before flowering. The small florets carry a light, sweet fragrance and bloom over a long season from late spring into summer, especially with regular deadheading. It performs as a short-lived perennial, generally staying vigorous for two to three years before benefiting from replacement.

common_name: Green Trick Dianthus (Novelty Green Pompom Sweet William)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Green Trick is a novelty sweet william grown for its unusual green pompom flower heads rather than colorful petals.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Green Trick is a novelty Sweet William grown not for colorful petals but for its unusual, fully double, bright green pompom-like flower clusters, formed from proliferated calyxes rather than typical petals, giving the plant an almost artificial, textural appearance prized in cut-flower arrangements and bouquets. It produces little to no fragrance, distinguishing it from clove-scented traditional sweet williams, and the long-lasting flower heads hold their green color well after cutting. Propagated by division or tissue culture rather than seed, it is grown as a florist crop as much as a garden perennial.

common_name: Scent First Coral Reef Dianthus (Extra-Fragrant Coral-Pink Garden Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Scent First Coral Reef is part of a Proven Winners perennial pink series specifically bred for strong clove fragrance.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Scent First Coral Reef is part of a Proven Winners perennial pink series specifically bred to combine strong, sweet clove fragrance with reliable garden performance, producing semi-double, coral-pink flowers with a darker pink eye above a neat mound of blue-green foliage. It blooms heavily in spring and continues intermittently into summer with deadheading, holding up to heat and humidity better than many older fragrant pink cultivars. Like other dianthus, it needs sharp drainage and resents wet, heavy soil.

common_name: Fruit Punch Maraschino Cherry Dianthus (Proven Winners Deep Red Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Maraschino Cherry is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for improved heat tolerance and repeat bloom.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Maraschino Cherry, part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series, bears semi-double, rich cherry-red flowers with a subtle darker red eye held above a compact mound of blue-green foliage, opening in flushes from spring through summer with deadheading. Like other Fruit Punch series dianthus it carries a light, sweet fragrance and shows improved heat tolerance and repeat bloom compared to older garden pink cultivars. It performs best in sharply drained, lean to average soil and resents soggy conditions.

common_name: Fruit Punch Black Cherry Frost Dianthus (Proven Winners Dark Maroon-Red Interspecific Pink)
scientific_name: Dianthus interspecific 'Fruit Punch Black Cherry Frost'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Black Cherry Frost is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for improved heat tolerance and repeat bloom.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Black Cherry Frost, part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series, produces semi-double flowers in a deep, dark maroon-red with a faint icy picotee edge on the petals, a striking dark color unusual among garden pinks, held above a compact mound of blue-green foliage. It blooms in flushes from spring through summer with deadheading, carries a light sweet fragrance, and shows better summer heat tolerance and repeat flowering than many older dianthus cultivars. It needs sharp drainage and lean to average soil to perform its best.

common_name: Paint the Town Magenta Dianthus (Proven Winners Vivid Magenta Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Paint the Town Magenta is a Proven Winners dianthus bred for cutting-length stems and a long bloom season.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Paint the Town Magenta bears masses of single to semi-double, vivid magenta-pink flowers on a vigorous, mounding plant, part of a Proven Winners dianthus series bred for extended cutting-length stems and a long bloom season from spring into summer. It carries a light, sweet clove fragrance and rebounds well after deadheading or a midseason shear, maintaining a tidy mound. Like other dianthus it requires sharp drainage and lean to average soil, resenting wet, heavy ground.
